children: Despite fears the midterm election results may lead to a slowdown in data-center development, Siebert Williams Shank analysts say in a note that state and local policy will play a larger role in directing the pace of the AI buildout than Congress. Moreover, the analysts say, states and municipalities have found successful models for data-center development that meet policy objectives, as in Louisiana. They predict states without clear policies around data centers will increasingly adopt them by the middle of next year. "As these local processes and regulations are established, we expect data center construction to gain further tangible momentum," the analysts say.(elias.schisgall@wsj.com)
